newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland plans to allow more foreign borrowing in 97.
newsitem.headline: Poland plans to allow more foreign borrowing in 97.

text.p: Poland plans to increase the amount it can borrow internationally to three billion zlotys in 1997 from a 1.39 billion limit in 1996, a deputy finance minister said on Wednesday.

"Inflows from foreign borrowing in 1997 cannot top three billion zlotys...This could be either Eurobonds or other borrowing," Halina Wasilewska-Trenkner told a news conference on the government's proposals for next year's budget.
Poland has tapped international markets twice over the last two years, and has earmarked its next international bond placement for the end of the second quarter of 1997.

The government draft currently assumes next year's budget deficit will be 2.6 percent of gross domestic product and personal income tax levels will remain flat at this year's levels of 21, 33, and 45 percent.
She said the deficit total would rise to 11.3 billion zlotys, up from the 10.16 billion planned in 1996, and state spending would rise to 127 billion from 110 billion.

Wasilewska-Trenkner said Poland's non-banking sector should finance between 4.5 billion and 6.0 billion zlotys of the 1997 budget deficit while domestic banks should finance between 6.7 billion and 8.2 billion.

She said the government's goals for 1997 were largely consistent with those set by the National Bank of Poland, which has often voiced concern over inflationary financing of the budget deficit by domestic banks.

Wasilewska-Trenkner said the budget plan saw Poland's gross domestic product rising by at least 5.5 percent next year and inflation falling to a year-on-year 13 percent in December 1997 compared with 19.5 percent in September this year.

She said that under the budget plan real wages would rise by 3.5 percent next year, although government employee's wages would be frozen in real terms, and that investment would increase by some 13.5 percent in 1997.
She said that if the Polish government's plan to cut taxes to 20, 31, 43 percent next year was realised, the budget deficit would rise an additional 1.9 billion zlotys.
If a four-level tax scale recently passed by the lower house of parliament went into effect, the deficit would rise by an additional 3.5 billion zlotys next year.
The government, which opposes the four-level scale introducing a 17 percent tax band for the lowest-paid, hopes this scheme will be blocked in the upper house, the Senate.
The government has said it will amend its budget draft, which is already before parliament, if its own proposals for a limited tax cut are passed.

Poland's 1996 sovereign debt issue was rated as BBB minus by Standard & Poor's and BB plus by IBCA. Moody's Investors Service last year rated Poland's sovereign debt as Baa3. -- Wojciech Moskwa +48 22 653 9700
